title: One-page pitch: why a community makerspace needs a CNC router
summary: A persuasive one-pager for a makerspace board: evidence, costs, and member outcomes for adding a CNC router.

blocks.title: Add a CNC router: more members finishing real projects
blocks.body: A mid-size community makerspace already has saws and a laser. A CNC router closes the gap between 'I designed it' and 'I cut the furniture / sign / robot base.' This page is the board pitch — evidence first, romance second.

blocks.heading: Evidence the board can check
rows: Bits, dust collection filters, maintenance hours
blocks.caption: Replace example numbers with your space's poll before the meeting.

blocks.heading: Example budget band
rows: Bed size matched to sheet goods members buy

blocks.heading: Member outcomes (why this is not a toy)

items.label: Furniture and cabinets leave the shop finished
Robotics / art / signage share one platform
CAD skills become physical
items.detail: Closes the 'designed forever, built never' leak.

items.label: Class revenue + retention
items.detail: Badge classes and advanced CAM nights.

columns.name: Safety / noise / dust
columns.detail: Enclosed or curtain area, dust collection interlock, badge required, hours policy — same playbook as the table saw, written down.

columns.name: We have a laser
columns.detail: Different thickness, joinery, and materials. Complementary, not redundant.

blocks.heading: The ask
blocks.body: Approve a not-to-exceed purchase in the example band, name a machine captain, and schedule the first badge class within 30 days of delivery.

blocks.title: Tone for the meeting
blocks.body: Lead with unfinished member projects and utilization math. Save the shiny spindle video for the appendix.
